numbers.quote: latent chain-of-thought improves over the baseline on 7/9 time-series datasets (+12.63\% average gain) and 23/27 tabular datasets (+3.25\% average gain)

survey_notes: One of the few papers in this group that directly compares sequence-axis latent CoT against a weight-tied looped transformer and an effective-depth-matched deeper model; reports CoT best on average. Whether the looped baseline was compute-matched is not stated in the abstract. Full text exists, not read per assignment; lead should extract the looped-vs-CoT numbers.

title: ARC Prize 2025: Technical Report

one_sentence: Report on ARC Prize 2025 (ARC-AGI-2): top Kaggle score 24%, refinement loops as the year's defining theme, including weight-space refinement by tiny zero-pretraining networks, and knowledge-dependent overfitting in frontier models.

claims.evidence_quote: The defining theme of 2025 is the emergence of the refinement loop -- a per-task iterative program optimization loop guided by a feedback signal.

claims.claim: Refinement in weight space by zero-pretraining deep learning methods reaches competitive results with very small (7M-parameter) networks.
claims.evidence_quote: Such refinement loops are also possible in weight space, as evidenced by zero-pretraining deep learning methods which are now achieving competitive performance with remarkably small networks (7M parameters).

title: The Depth Ceiling: On the Limits of Large Language Models in Discovering Latent Planning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: On graph path-finding with controlled latent planning depth, models trained only on final answers discover strategies of at most 3 (tiny from-scratch) to 5 (fine-tuned GPT-4o, Qwen3-32B) latent steps, though discovered strategies execute up to 8 steps at test time.

claims.claim: Discoverable latent planning depth is small: 3 steps for tiny from-scratch transformers, 5 for fine-tuned GPT-4o/Qwen3-32B, 7 for GPT-5.4 few-shot.
claims.evidence_quote: tiny transformers trained from scratch discover strategies requiring up to three latent steps, fine-tuned GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B reach five, and GPT-5.4 attains seven under few-shot prompting.

claims.claim: Strategies learned up to 5 steps generalize up to 8 steps at test time, dissociating discovery from execution.
claims.evidence_quote: Although the maximum latent planning depth models can learn during training is five, the discovered strategy generalizes up to eight latent steps at test-time.

numbers.what: max latent steps discovered: tiny / fine-tuned frontier / GPT-5.4 few-shot
numbers.quote: tiny transformers trained from scratch discover strategies requiring up to three latent steps, fine-tuned GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B reach five, and GPT-5.4 attains seven under few-shot prompting.

survey_notes: Benchmark-style evidence of a latent depth ceiling in standard Transformers; a natural testbed for looped models (does looping raise the discoverable depth?). Relevant to CoT-monitorability argument (2507.11473). Abstract only.

title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: REST adds four differentiable representation losses (causality, minimality, separability, stability) to cross-entropy for latent thoughts in recurrent single-agent and multi-agent systems, improving accuracy at equal data, compute and latent budget.

claims.claim: CE-only training of latent thoughts has failure modes such as collapsing thoughts across questions and retaining irrelevant information.
claims.evidence_quote: Theoretical and empirical analyses establish and confirm four failures of CE-only training that lead to a lower probability of the correct answer such as collapsing thoughts across distinct questions and retaining irrelevant information.

claims.claim: At equal data, compute and latent budget, REST improves accuracy by up to 7.5 points and convergence by 30%.
claims.evidence_quote: with the same training data, compute, and latent budget, REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30\%.

numbers.what: max accuracy gain over CE-only; convergence gain
numbers.quote: REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30\%.

survey_notes: Thought-collapse diagnosis parallels SIM-CoT (2509.20317). Applies to systems 'recurring on their own hidden states'; the losses could transfer to per-loop states of looped models. Abstract only.

title: Learned Relay Representations for Forward-Thinking Discrete Diffusion Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (diffusion_and_iterative_refinement); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Relay adds a differentiable per-token channel that carries latent information between masked-diffusion denoising passes, trained with truncated BPTT; on Fast-dLLM v2 it beats standard SFT on coding while cutting latency up to 32%.

claims.claim: Relay passes latent information between forward passes through a per-token channel trained by truncated BPTT.
claims.evidence_quote: Relay introduces a differentiable per-token channel that passes information between forward passes and is trained via truncated backpropagation through time (BPTT).

claims.claim: On Fast-dLLM v2, Relay outperforms standard SFT on coding while reducing latency by up to 32%.
claims.evidence_quote: We then scale Relay to Fast-dLLM v2, a state-of-the-art DLM, outperforming standard supervised finetuning on coding tasks while reducing inference latency by up to 32%.

numbers.what: inference latency reduction
numbers.quote: outperforming standard supervised finetuning on coding tasks while reducing inference latency by up to 32%.

survey_notes: Turns diffusion denoising into a recurrent latent loop (state carried across passes), making DLMs structurally close to looped models with input injection; same truncated-BPTT trade-off as looped training. Abstract only.

title: LLM Reasoning Is Latent, Not the Chain of Thought
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (prior_surveys_and_positions); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Position paper arguing LLM reasoning should be studied as latent-state trajectory formation, contrasting H1 (latent trajectories), H2 (surface CoT) and H0 (generic serial compute), and calling for evaluations that disentangle surface traces, latent states and serial compute.

claims.claim: H0 is that most apparent reasoning gains come from generic serial compute rather than a privileged representation.
claims.evidence_quote: H0, most apparent reasoning gains are better explained by generic serial compute than by any privileged representational object.

claims.claim: Current evidence most strongly supports H1 (latent-state trajectories) as a default working hypothesis.
claims.evidence_quote: we find that current evidence most strongly supports H1 as a default working hypothesis rather than as a task-independent verdict.

claims.claim: Evaluations should disentangle surface traces, latent states and serial compute.
claims.evidence_quote: it should evaluate reasoning with designs that explicitly disentangle surface traces, latent states, and serial compute.

survey_notes: Methodological ally of our regime audit: matched serial-compute budgets are needed to separate representation from compute (H0). Looped models are a clean way to add serial compute without surface tokens. Abstract only.

title: Latent Reasoning with Supervised Thinking States
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Thinking States generates short thinking-token sequences every few input tokens, maps them back to embeddings added to subsequent inputs, and trains them with natural-language supervision via parallel teacher forcing; it extrapolates better than CoT on state tracking.

claims.claim: Thoughts are generated every few input tokens and added back into the following input embeddings.
claims.evidence_quote: Thinking States generates sequences of thinking tokens every few input tokens, transforms the thoughts back into embedding space, and adds them to the following input tokens.

claims.claim: Because thoughts are tokens, they can be supervised with natural language and trained by parallel teacher forcing.
claims.evidence_quote: since the thoughts are represented as tokens, they can be learned from natural language supervision, and using teacher-forcing, which is parallelizable.

claims.claim: On state tracking, Thinking States extrapolates to longer sequences than seen in training, beating CoT.
claims.evidence_quote: On state-tracking tasks, we show Thinking States leads to stronger reasoning behavior than CoT, successfully extrapolating to longer sequences than seen during training.

survey_notes: Interleaves recurrence with input processing (reasoning during prefill), a different placement of extra compute than looping or Coconut. Abstract only.

title: T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: T2MLR fuses a cached middle-layer representation of the previous token into an earlier layer of the current token, giving cross-time latent recurrence at low inference cost; it beats data- and parameter-matched baselines and middle-block recurrence beats full-layer recurrence.

claims.claim: T2MLR outperforms data- and parameter-matched Transformer baselines in pretraining and multi-hop finetuning.
claims.evidence_quote: Across natural-language pretraining and multi-hop reasoning finetuning, T2MLR consistently outperforms data- and parameter-matched Transformer base lines.

claims.claim: Recurring through only a localized middle-layer block (as little as 20% of the network) often beats full-layer recurrence.
claims.evidence_quote: applying recurrence to only a localized middle-layer block (as little as 20% of the network) often outperforms full-layer recurrence.

claims.claim: The authors conclude effective latent reasoning does not require looping over all layers.
claims.evidence_quote: These results suggest that effective latent reasoning in Transformers does not require looping over all layers as in previous works, but can instead emerge more strongly from targeted middle-layer recurrence.

numbers.what: fraction of network in recurrent block that can suffice
numbers.quote: applying recurrence to only a localized middle-layer block (as little as 20% of the network) often outperforms full-layer recurrence.

survey_notes: Directly speaks to looped-model design: partial (middle-block) recurrence beats whole-stack recurrence, consistent with sandwich/prelude-core-coda findings in looped models, but here the recurrence is across time (previous token) rather than within a token. Retrofit into a pretrained 1.7B model per abstract. Full text exists, not read per assignment.

title: Pretraining with Token-Level Adaptive Latent Chain-of-Thought
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Adaptive latent CoT pretraining lets the model generate a variable-length latent trajectory before each token, with token-wise adaptive halting emerging from one-stage pretraining; it improves perplexity and downstream accuracy with fewer training FLOPs than prior recurrent baselines.

claims.claim: The work frames per-token computation without extra parameters as an alternative scaling axis.
claims.evidence_quote: This work explores an alternative axis: increasing per-token computation without expanding parameters, by internalizing latent Chain-of-Thought (CoT) into pretraining.

claims.claim: Longer latent trajectories are allocated to difficult tokens and shorter (or zero) to easy ones.
claims.evidence_quote: allocating longer trajectories to difficult tokens and shorter (or even zero) trajectories to easy ones.

claims.claim: It improves perplexity and downstream accuracy even with fewer training FLOPs than prior recurrent baselines.
claims.evidence_quote: Experiments with Llama architectures show that adaptive latent CoT consistently improves language modeling perplexity and broad downstream accuracy, even with fewer training FLOPs than prior recurrent baselines.

survey_notes: Same 'third axis without parameters' pitch as looped LMs, realized on the sequence axis with learned halting. Which recurrent baselines were used (possibly looped models) is not in the abstract; lead should check. Abstract only.

title: Forward-Free Diffusion Language Models with BPTT-Free Looped Refinement
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (diffusion_and_iterative_refinement); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: FReDA drops the hand-designed forward corruption process: model-generated drafts serve as intermediate states and a refinement model is trained by backpropagating only through the final refinement pass; FReDA-4B beats larger diffusion base models on reasoning and coding.

claims.claim: Training detaches earlier refinement passes and backpropagates only through the last pass, avoiding BPTT.
claims.evidence_quote: Training detaches the preceding refinement passes and backpropagates only through the final pass, avoiding backpropagation through time (BPTT) across refinement iterations while retaining standard backpropagation within the final Transformer pass.

claims.claim: FReDA-4B outperforms larger diffusion base models with up to 15% absolute gains and 1.5-1.8x speedup.
claims.evidence_quote: FReDA-4B outperforms larger diffusion base models on reasoning and coding benchmarks, achieving absolute gains of up to 15%, while reaching a 1.5-1.8x average speedup over diffusion baselines and scaling effectively with additional refinement computation.

numbers.what: max absolute gain; speedup over diffusion baselines
numbers.quote: achieving absolute gains of up to 15%, while reaching a 1.5-1.8x average speedup over diffusion baselines

survey_notes: Looped refinement in output space with last-pass-only gradients: the diffusion analogue of one-step / last-step gradient training in looped and recursive-reasoning models. Comparison against larger models is unmatched. Abstract only.

title: Turbo Connection: Reasoning as Information Flow from Higher to Lower Layers
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: TurboConn routes dense residual connections from higher-layer states of token t to lower layers of token t+1, lifting the fixed-depth limit on latent computation paths; fine-tuned into pretrained LLMs it improves GSM8K, Parity and arithmetic, e.g. Qwen-3-1.7B Parity from 53.78% to 100%.

claims.claim: Multiple residual connections route higher-layer states of token t into lower layers of token t+1.
claims.evidence_quote: routing multiple residual connections from the higher-layer hidden states of each token $t$ to the lower layers of token $t+1$.

claims.claim: Adding TurboConn to a fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B raises Parity from 53.78% to 100%.
claims.evidence_quote: while a fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B achieves only 53.78% on Parity, adding our architectural modification enables the model to reach 100% accuracy

claims.claim: Dense backward connections significantly outperform sparse single-vector feedback.
claims.evidence_quote: our dense interaction significantly outperforms "sparse" alternatives that only pass a single hidden state or vector.

numbers.what: Parity accuracy of fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B without vs with TurboConn
numbers.quote: while a fine-tuned Qwen-3-1.7B achieves only 53.78% on Parity, adding our architectural modification enables the model to reach 100% accuracy

numbers.what: benchmark gains range
numbers.quote: yields accuracy gains of 0.9% to over 10% on benchmarks like GSM8K, Parity, and multi-step arithmetic

survey_notes: Deep-to-shallow cross-time feedback (like full-bandwidth 2608.08888, T2MLR 2607.15178, LIFT 2609.38149). 'Dense beats sparse feedback' contrasts with Coconut's single-vector feedback. Abstract only.

title: Parallel Scaling Law for Language Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: ParScale reuses parameters across P learnable input transformations run in parallel and aggregated, proposing a scaling law where P streams act like O(log P) more parameters with better inference memory and latency than parameter scaling.

claims.claim: ParScale is presented as a third, inference-efficient scaling paradigm: more parallel computation in training and inference.
claims.evidence_quote: We introduce the third and more inference-efficient scaling paradigm: increasing the model's parallel computation during both training and inference time.

claims.claim: P parallel streams behave like scaling parameters by O(log P).
claims.evidence_quote: a model with $P$ parallel streams is similar to scaling the parameters by $O(\log P)$ while showing superior inference efficiency.

claims.claim: For the same improvement, ParScale needs up to 22x less memory increase and 6x less latency increase than parameter scaling.
claims.evidence_quote: ParScale can use up to 22$\times$ less memory increase and 6$\times$ less latency increase compared to parameter scaling that achieves the same performance improvement.

numbers.what: memory and latency increase advantage vs parameter scaling
numbers.value: 22x less memory increase; 6x less latency increase
numbers.quote: ParScale can use up to 22$\times$ less memory increase and 6$\times$ less latency increase compared to parameter scaling

survey_notes: Competing 'third scaling axis' claim: parallel (width-wise) parameter reuse vs the survey's serial (depth-wise) parameter reuse. The survey should acknowledge this naming conflict and contrast parallel vs serial reuse (latency profile, expressivity per 2503.03961/2505.21024). Abstract only.

title: Coevolutionary Continuous Discrete Diffusion: Make Your Diffusion Language Model a Latent Reasoner
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (diffusion_and_iterative_refinement); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: CCDD runs a joint diffusion over continuous representations and discrete tokens with one model, motivated by a proof that continuous diffusion is more expressive than discrete diffusion and looped transformers, and reports strong language-modeling results.

claims.claim: Continuous diffusion models are proven to have stronger expressivity than discrete diffusion and looped transformers.
claims.evidence_quote: In particular, we prove that continuous diffusion models have stronger expressivity than discrete diffusions and looped transformers.

claims.claim: Continuous diffusion offers intermediate supervision that looped transformers lack, but decoding continuous states to tokens is hard; CCDD combines both spaces.
claims.evidence_quote: while continuous diffusion provides intermediate supervision that looped transformers lack, they introduce additional difficulty decoding tokens into the discrete token space from the continuous representation space.

survey_notes: Explicit theoretical comparison with looped transformers: claims continuous diffusion is strictly more expressive and that looped models lack intermediate supervision (relevant to deep-supervision designs in looped/recursive models). Full text exists, not read per assignment; lead should check the exact theorem statement and assumptions.

title: Soft Tokens, Hard Truths
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Learns continuous CoT with RL using soft tokens (token mixtures plus input-embedding noise), scaling to hundreds of latent tokens on Llama/Qwen up to 8B; matches discrete CoT at pass@1 and beats it at pass@32, and best deployment is soft training with hard inference.

claims.claim: Continuous-CoT RL matches discrete-token CoT at pass@1 and beats it at pass@32 on math with models up to 8B.
claims.evidence_quote: On math reasoning benchmarks with Llama and Qwen models up to 8B, training with continuous CoTs match discrete-token CoTs for pass@1 and surpass them for pass@32, showing greater CoT diversity.

claims.claim: The best setting is to train with continuous CoT and infer with discrete tokens.
claims.evidence_quote: the best-performing scenario is to train with continuous CoT tokens then use discrete tokens for inference, meaning the "soft" models can be deployed in a standard way.

claims.claim: This is presented as the first scalable RL method for continuous CoTs without distillation from discrete CoTs.
claims.evidence_quote: This is the first work introducing a scalable method to learn continuous CoTs via reinforcement learning (RL), without distilling from reference discrete CoTs.

survey_notes: Shows continuous thoughts can be learned by RL rather than CoT distillation; the soft-train/hard-infer result suggests the benefit may come from training dynamics rather than latent inference itself. Abstract only.

title: The Serial Scaling Hypothesis
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (prior_surveys_and_positions); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Position/theory paper formalizing inherently serial problems in complexity terms, arguing parallel-centric architectures are fundamentally limited on them and showing diffusion models cannot solve inherently serial problems.

claims.claim: Diffusion models, despite their iterative nature, cannot solve inherently serial problems.
claims.evidence_quote: we show for first time that diffusion models despite their sequential nature are incapable of solving inherently serial problems.

claims.claim: Inherently serial problems need sequentially dependent steps that cannot be efficiently parallelized.
claims.evidence_quote: require sequentially dependent computational steps that cannot be efficiently parallelized.

survey_notes: Supports serial compute (CoT or depth recurrence) as necessary for some tasks. Contradicts the framing of diffusion as 'infinite-depth reasoning' in 2507.06203 Sec. 5. Whether looped models count as serial depends on loop count scaling with input (see 2609.33134). Abstract only.

title: Catch Your Breath: Adaptive Computation for Self-Paced Sequence Production
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: CYB trains a model to request extra pause steps per token by emitting a <don't know> output, framed as sequential decision making, outperforming standard cross-entropy pause training in pretraining and finetuning.

claims.claim: The model signals it needs more compute by emitting <don't know>, delaying its response via a pause, possibly repeatedly.
claims.evidence_quote: The model indicates the need for additional compute steps by emitting a special <don't know> output, delaying its response via a pause.

claims.claim: CYB beats standard cross-entropy in pretraining or finetuning, lowering perplexity and raising downstream accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: Our experiments demonstrate that CYB significantly outperforms standard cross-entropy when introduced either in pretraining or fine-tuning, reducing perplexity and enhancing downstream accuracy with no additional computational or memory cost.

survey_notes: Sequence-axis learned halting (per-token pause count), the analogue of ACT-style halting over loops. The 'no additional cost' claim refers to the loss relative to CE pause training, not to models without pauses. Abstract only.

title: Energy-Based Transformers are Scalable Learners and Thinkers
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (deep_equilibrium_and_implicit); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: EBTs learn an energy over (input, candidate prediction) pairs and predict by gradient-descent energy minimization; they report faster training scaling than Transformer++ and larger gains from extra inference-time optimization on language tasks.

claims.claim: Predictions are made by gradient-descent energy minimization until convergence.
claims.evidence_quote: enabling predictions through gradient descent-based energy minimization until convergence.

claims.claim: EBTs scale up to 35% faster than Transformer++ across data, batch size, parameters, FLOPs and depth.
claims.evidence_quote: we find EBTs scale faster than the dominant Transformer++ approach during training, achieving an up to 35% higher scaling rate with respect to data, batch size, parameters, FLOPs, and depth.

claims.claim: Extra inference-time thinking improves EBTs 29% more than Transformer++ on language tasks.
claims.evidence_quote: During inference, EBTs improve performance with System 2 Thinking by 29% more than the Transformer++ on language tasks

numbers.what: higher scaling rate vs Transformer++
numbers.quote: achieving an up to 35% higher scaling rate with respect to data, batch size, parameters, FLOPs, and depth

numbers.what: extra gain from System 2 thinking vs Transformer++
numbers.quote: EBTs improve performance with System 2 Thinking by 29% more than the Transformer++ on language tasks

survey_notes: Optimization-based iterative inference (prediction refined by gradient steps on an energy) as a neighbor of fixed-point/looped refinement; Coconut's authors list it as a scalable latent method to integrate. Scaling-rate comparisons need regime scrutiny. Abstract only.

title: A Survey on Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models: What, How, Where, and How Well?
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (prior_surveys_and_positions); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Survey of test-time scaling organized along what, how, where and how well to scale, with deployment guidelines and open challenges.

claims.claim: The survey's framework uses four dimensions: what, how, where and how well to scale.
claims.evidence_quote: we propose a unified, multidimensional framework structured along four core dimensions of TTS research: what to scale, how to scale, where to scale, and how well to scale.

survey_notes: Prior TTS survey; looped models add a latent 'what to scale' option (depth) to its token- and sample-based axes. Abstract only.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: DeepSeek-R1 shows reasoning can be incentivized by pure RL without human-labeled reasoning traces, yielding emergent self-reflection and verification, with distillation of the patterns into smaller models.

claims.claim: Reasoning can be incentivized through pure RL without human-labeled reasoning trajectories.
claims.evidence_quote: Here we show that the reasoning abilities of LLMs can be incentivized through pure reinforcement learning (RL), obviating the need for human-labeled reasoning trajectories.

claims.claim: RL produces emergent reasoning patterns such as self-reflection and verification.
claims.evidence_quote: The proposed RL framework facilitates the emergent development of advanced reasoning patterns, such as self-reflection, verification, and dynamic strategy adaptation.

survey_notes: Reference point for token-axis test-time compute (long CoT via RL). 2512.14064 finds long-CoT models do not increase effective depth, i.e. this axis adds serial steps through tokens, not per-token depth. Abstract only.

title: Dream 7B: Diffusion Large Language Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (diffusion_and_iterative_refinement); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Dream 7B is an open discrete-diffusion LLM that refines sequences in parallel by iterative denoising, initialized from an AR LLM with context-adaptive token-level noise rescheduling, outperforming prior diffusion LMs.

claims.claim: Dream 7B refines sequences in parallel through iterative denoising.
claims.evidence_quote: Dream 7B employs discrete diffusion modeling to refine sequences in parallel through iterative denoising.

claims.claim: Training relies on AR-LLM initialization and context-adaptive token-level noise rescheduling.
claims.evidence_quote: These results are achieved through simple yet effective training techniques, including AR-based LLM initialization and context-adaptive token-level noise rescheduling.

claims.claim: Dream offers tunable quality-speed trade-offs, infilling and arbitrary-order generation.
claims.evidence_quote: inference flexibility, including arbitrary-order generation, infilling capabilities, and tunable quality-speed trade-offs.

title: Language models can learn implicit multi-hop reasoning, but only if they have lots of training data
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: GPT-2-style models trained from scratch on k-hop data can learn implicit k-hop reasoning, but required data grows exponentially and required layers grow linearly in k; curriculum learning reduces but does not remove the data need.

claims.claim: Implicit k-hop reasoning needs training data exponential in k and layers linear in k.
claims.evidence_quote: while such models can indeed learn implicit $k$-hop reasoning, the required training data grows exponentially in $k$, and the required number of transformer layers grows linearly in $k$.

claims.claim: Curriculum learning mitigates but does not eliminate the data requirement.
claims.evidence_quote: We further find that the data requirement can be mitigated, but not eliminated, through curriculum learning.

survey_notes: Layers-linear-in-hops is the cleanest motivation for adding depth by looping; the exponential data cost is a hypothesis looped models can test (does weight sharing lower it?). Agrees with 2402.16837 and 2405.15071. Abstract only.

title: Emergence of Superposition: Unveiling the Training Dynamics of Chain of Continuous Thought
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Training-dynamics analysis of a two-layer Transformer with continuous CoT on graph reachability shows the index-matching logit first grows then stays bounded, which balances exploration and exploitation and yields superposition of search traces.

claims.claim: The index-matching logit increases and then remains bounded during continuous-thought training.
claims.evidence_quote: the index-matching logit, an important quantity which reflects the strength of the model's local search ability, will first increase and then remain bounded under mild assumptions.

claims.claim: Bounded logits make the model weight several plausible traces comparably under uncertainty, i.e. superposition.
claims.evidence_quote: assign comparable weights to multiple such traces to explore when it is uncertain about which solution is correct, which results in superposition.

survey_notes: Theory support for Coconut's BFS claim; contrast with 2604.06374's empirical collapse in fine-tuned regimes. Abstract only.

title: Parallel Continuous Chain-of-Thought with Jacobi Iteration
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: PCCoT updates all latent thought tokens in parallel by Jacobi iteration instead of sequentially, matching or beating sequential continuous CoT while saving nearly 50% of training and inference time and training more stably.

claims.claim: PCCoT performs Jacobi iteration on latent thought tokens, updating them in parallel.
claims.evidence_quote: we propose Parallel Continuous Chain-of-Thought (PCCoT), which performs Jacobi iteration on the latent thought tokens, updating them iteratively in parallel instead of sequentially

claims.claim: With a suitable number of iterations it is comparable or better while saving nearly 50% of training and inference time.
claims.evidence_quote: by choosing the proper number of iterations, we are able to achieve comparable or even better performance while saving nearly 50% of the training and inference time.

numbers.what: training and inference time saved
numbers.quote: saving nearly 50% of the training and inference time

survey_notes: Key bridge between families: Jacobi iteration turns a sequence-axis latent chain into a fixed number of parallel refinement iterations over a block of latent tokens, i.e. a loop over passes of the whole model, structurally like looping or diffusion refinement. Abstract only.

title: What Affects the Effective Depth of Large Language Models?
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Study of effective depth across Qwen-2.5 1.5B-32B, base vs long-CoT models and task difficulty: effective layers grow with size but the ratio is stable, long-CoT training does not raise effective depth, and harder tasks do not use more layers.

claims.claim: Effective layers grow with model size while the effective depth ratio stays stable.
claims.evidence_quote: we analyze the model behavior of Qwen-2.5 family (1.5B-32B) and find that while the number of effective layers grows with model size, the effective depth ratio remains stable.

claims.claim: Long-CoT models show no increase in effective depth over their base models.
claims.evidence_quote: comparisons between base and corresponding long-CoT models show no increase in effective depth, suggesting that improved reasoning stems from longer context rather than deeper per-token computation.

claims.claim: Models do not use more layers for harder problems.
claims.evidence_quote: evaluations across tasks of varying difficulty indicate that models do not dynamically use more layers for harder problems.

builds_on: Do Language Models Use Their Depth Efficiently? (2505.13898)
survey_notes: Replicates and extends 2505.13898 (effective depth concept) to Qwen-2.5 up to 32B and long-CoT models; the long-CoT result separates token-axis compute from per-token depth, which is the axis looped models target. Partially contradicted by 2604.12426 (finetuned models do adapt depth). Abstract only.

title: The Curse of Depth in Large Language Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (depth_use_analyses); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Attributes the ineffectiveness of nearly half the layers in modern LLMs to Pre-LN output variance growing with depth (deep blocks near identity) and proposes LayerNorm Scaling, which improves pretraining from 130M to 7B.

claims.claim: Pre-LN is identified as the cause of ineffective deep layers.
claims.evidence_quote: identifies that the underlying reason for the ineffectiveness of deep layers in LLMs is the widespread usage of Pre-Layer Normalization (Pre-LN).

claims.claim: LayerNorm Scaling consistently improves pretraining across 130M-7B models.
claims.evidence_quote: Across a wide range of model sizes (130M to 7B), our experiments show that LNS consistently outperforms previous normalization and scaling techniques in enhancing LLM pre-training performance.

survey_notes: Competing explanation for under-used late layers: normalization/variance (architecture) rather than objective or ensemble behavior (2505.13898 discusses residual norm growth; 2602.05970 proposes ensemble averaging). For looped models, residual growth across loops is the same issue, motivating normalization between loops. The state_passing tag is a design-relevance tag, not a looped mechanism. Abstract only.

title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (adaptive_depth_without_sharing); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: LayerSkip trains with depth-increasing layer dropout and a shared early-exit loss, then decodes by exiting early and verifying with the remaining layers (self-speculative decoding), reaching up to 2.16x speedup.

claims.claim: Training uses layer dropout increasing with depth plus an early-exit loss with a shared exit.
claims.evidence_quote: during training we apply layer dropout, with low dropout rates for earlier layers and higher dropout rates for later layers, and an early exit loss where all transformer layers share the same exit.

claims.claim: Self-speculative decoding gives up to 2.16x on CNN/DM summarization, 1.82x on coding and 2.0x on TOPv2.
claims.evidence_quote: We implement our inference solution and show speedups of up to 2.16x on summarization for CNN/DM documents, 1.82x on coding, and 2.0x on TOPv2 semantic parsing task.

numbers.what: speedups
numbers.quote: show speedups of up to 2.16x on summarization for CNN/DM documents, 1.82x on coding, and 2.0x on TOPv2 semantic parsing task.

survey_notes: Unshared precursor of self-speculative decoding for looped models (draft with fewer loops, verify with more); corpus has looped-specific versions (2609.17184 LoopSpec, 2609.23033 WaveFront, assigned to systems). Abstract only.

title: Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformer Language Models
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Transformers can use meaningless filler tokens instead of CoT to solve two hard algorithmic tasks, but learning to use fillers needs dense supervision; theory characterizes when fillers help via quantifier depth.

claims.claim: Filler tokens can replace CoT on two hard algorithmic tasks that cannot be solved without intermediate tokens.
claims.evidence_quote: transformers can use meaningless filler tokens (e.g., '......') in place of a chain of thought to solve two hard algorithmic tasks they could not solve when responding without intermediate tokens.

claims.claim: Learning to use filler tokens is hard and needs specific, dense supervision.
claims.evidence_quote: we find empirically that learning to use filler tokens is difficult and requires specific, dense supervision to converge.

survey_notes: Raises the auditability concern that also applies to looped models (hidden computation detached from visible tokens). Filler tokens add parallel positions, not serial depth; contrast with 2609.33134 (filler drives accuracy to the ceiling on serial tasks). Abstract only.

title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: Shows constant-depth, constant-precision Transformers without CoT are limited to AC0, while T CoT steps let them solve any problem computed by size-T boolean circuits; CoT strongly helps on parallel-hard tasks, especially for shallow models.

claims.claim: With T CoT steps, constant-depth constant-precision Transformers with O(log n) width solve any problem computable by size-T circuits.
claims.evidence_quote: with $T$ steps of CoT, constant-depth transformers using constant-bit precision and $O(\log n)$ embedding size can solve any problem solvable by boolean circuits of size $T$.

claims.claim: CoT dramatically helps on tasks hard for parallel computation, especially for low-depth Transformers.
claims.evidence_quote: enabling CoT dramatically improves the accuracy for tasks that are hard for parallel computation, including the composition of permutation groups, iterated squaring, and circuit value problems, especially for low-depth transformers.

survey_notes: Token-axis serial compute theory; the depth-axis counterpart (loops simulating CoT steps) is in the looped theory papers (e.g. 2502.17416, assigned to theory_a). Abstract only.

claims.claim: Generalized Kuramoto updates bind neurons through synchronization dynamics.
claims.evidence_quote: Our generalized Kuramoto updates bind neurons together through their synchronization dynamics.

claims.claim: The approach improves unsupervised object discovery, adversarial robustness, calibration and reasoning.
claims.evidence_quote: this idea provides performance improvements across a wide spectrum of tasks such as unsupervised object discovery, adversarial robustness, calibrated uncertainty quantification, and reasoning.

survey_notes: Iterative dynamical-system computation at the neuron level; peripheral neighbor of looped/equilibrium models (iterated updates of a state). Abstract only.

title: Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking

claims.evidence_quote: after continued pretraining of an LM on a corpus of internet text with Quiet-STaR, we find zero-shot improvements on GSM8K (5.9%$\rightarrow$10.9%) and CommonsenseQA (36.3%$\rightarrow$47.2%)

claims.claim: Generated rationales disproportionately help difficult-to-predict tokens.
claims.evidence_quote: generated rationales disproportionately help model difficult-to-predict tokens and improve the LM's ability to directly answer difficult questions.

numbers.what: zero-shot GSM8K and CommonsenseQA before/after
numbers.quote: we find zero-shot improvements on GSM8K (5.9%$\rightarrow$10.9%) and CommonsenseQA (36.3%$\rightarrow$47.2%)

title: On the Inductive Bias of Stacking Towards Improving Reasoning
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: MIDAS, a gradual-stacking variant, speeds LM training by up to 40% and shows an inductive bias toward reasoning tasks at similar or slightly worse perplexity, verified at 1B-8B and linked to looped models.

claims.claim: MIDAS improves reasoning-heavy downstream tasks despite similar or slightly worse perplexity.
claims.evidence_quote: MIDAS is not only training-efficient but surprisingly also has an inductive bias towards improving downstream tasks, especially tasks that require reasoning abilities like reading comprehension and math problems, despite having similar or slightly worse perplexity compared to baseline training.

claims.evidence_quote: we conjecture the underlying reason for this inductive bias by exploring the connection of stacking to looped models and provide strong supporting empirical analysis.

claims.evidence_quote: These findings of training efficiency and inductive bias towards reasoning are verified at 1B, 2B and 8B parameter language models.

Iso-data regime is my reading of 'compared to baseline training'; check full text. Abstract only.

title: Deliberation in Latent Space via Differentiable Cache Augmentation
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (sequence_axis_latent_reasoning); not a looped-depth model
one_sentence: A trained coprocessor augments a frozen LLM's KV cache with latent embeddings, learned end-to-end with the decoder's LM loss on pretraining data, lowering perplexity and improving reasoning tasks without task-specific training.

claims.evidence_quote: we demonstrate that a frozen LLM can be augmented with an offline coprocessor that operates on the model's key-value (kv) cache.

claims.evidence_quote: even without any task-specific training, our experiments demonstrate that cache augmentation consistently reduces perplexity and improves performance across a range of reasoning-intensive tasks.

title: Towards Revealing the Mystery behind Chain of Thought: A Theoretical Perspective

claims.evidence_quote: bounded-depth Transformers are unable to directly produce correct answers for basic arithmetic/equation tasks unless the model size grows super-polynomially with respect to the input length.

claims.claim: Constant-size autoregressive Transformers can solve these tasks by generating CoT derivations.
claims.evidence_quote: we then prove by construction that autoregressive Transformers of constant size suffice to solve both tasks by generating CoT derivations using a commonly used math language format.

survey_notes: Cited by Coconut for 'CoT increases effective depth because outputs are looped back to the input'. Theory baseline for comparing token-axis and depth-axis serial computation. Abstract only.

title: Transformers Learn to Achieve Second-Order Convergence Rates for In-Context Linear Regression
relevance_reason: neighboring paradigm (theory_scaling_and_depth_growth_background); not a looped-depth model

claims.evidence_quote: Empirically, predictions from successive Transformer layers closely match different iterations of Newton's Method linearly, with each middle layer roughly computing 3 iterations

claims.claim: Transformers can implement k Newton iterations with k + O(1) layers.
claims.evidence_quote: we prove that Transformers can implement $k$ iterations of Newton's method with $k + \mathcal{O}(1)$ layers.

title: Implicit Chain of Thought Reasoning via Knowledge Distillation

one_sentence: Implicit CoT distills a CoT-trained teacher so that reasoning happens 'vertically' across hidden states of different layers rather than 'horizontally' over generated tokens, solving multi-digit multiplication and GSM-style tasks at no-CoT speed.

claims.claim: Reasoning is distilled to happen vertically across layers' hidden states instead of horizontally across tokens.
claims.evidence_quote: instead of doing reasoning "horizontally" by producing intermediate words one-by-one, we distill it such that the reasoning happens "vertically" among the hidden states in different layers.

claims.claim: This enables solving tasks previously unsolvable without explicit CoT at no-CoT speed.
claims.evidence_quote: this approach enables solving tasks previously not solvable without explicit chain-of-thought, at a speed comparable to no chain-of-thought.

survey_notes: Origin of the horizontal/vertical vocabulary used by 2505.16782 and 2507.06203. 'Vertical' reasoning in a fixed-depth stack is bounded by layer count; looping is the way to extend that vertical budget. Abstract only.

title: The Impact of Depth on Compositional Generalization in Transformer Language Models

claims.evidence_quote: with a given total parameter budget, transformers can be made shallower than is typical without sacrificing performance.

title: The Parallelism Tradeoff: Limitations of Log-Precision Transformers

claims.claim: Any architecture as parallelizable as the Transformer is conjectured to share these limits.
claims.evidence_quote: We thus speculatively introduce the idea of a fundamental parallelism tradeoff: any model architecture as parallelizable as the transformer will obey limitations similar to it.

title: Looped Diffusion Transformer

claims.regime: iso_param; iso_infer_flop; iso_train_flop; iso_effective_depth (deeper baseline has 32 effective depth); same training data
claims.evidence_quote: Looped-DiT B/32 improves the average score by 4.0 points over the parameter-matched baseline and outperforms both inference-compute-matched baselines despite using fewer parameters. Under matched training compute, it achieves 59.1 compared with 58.1 for the deeper baseline.

claims.claim: At matched per-image inference FLOPs, spending compute on loop depth beats spending it on more denoising steps.
claims.evidence_quote: From 25- to 50-step settings, allocating compute to loop depth consistently yields higher performance than allocating it to additional denoising steps, showing that looping is a more effective use of inference compute.

claims.claim: Naive looping fails: performance saturates and declines beyond training depth while spatial position information erodes; this motivates deep supervision and attention modulation.
claims.evidence_quote: As shown in Fig. 3(b), R2 drops from 0.865 after the 1st loop to 0.562 after 8th loops, an absolute decrease of 0.303, indicating that spatial position becomes progressively less linearly decodable.

claims.claim: Against public checkpoints, the 260M looped model beats a 6.5x larger model at 4.9x lower inference compute (different training data and recipes).
claims.evidence_quote: Notably, a 260M-parameter Looped-DiT outperforms non-looped models with roughly 6.5× more parameters across multiple text-to-image benchmarks while requiring 4.9× lower inference compute.

claims.claim: Looping and textual CoT prompt rewriting are complementary: looping helps constraint-resolution subtasks, CoT helps inferring implied content.
claims.regime: same checkpoint family; unclear compute matching
claims.evidence_quote: Consistent with the constraint-resolution and self-correction behavior observed above, Tab. 3 shows larger gains from looping on subtasks that require joint satisfaction of relational, procedural, or spatial constraints.

numbers.what: Table 2 avg score (B/32): param-matched MiniT2I B/32 vs Looped-DiT B/32
numbers.quote: Under matched training compute, it achieves 59.1 compared with 58.1 for the deeper baseline.

numbers.what: XSA gain for looped vs non-looped baselines
numbers.quote: Tab. 5 shows that XSA yields a larger gain for the looped model (+1.6) than for the parameter-matched (−0.1) and compute-matched (+0.7) non-looped baselines

numbers.what: Adaptive looping vs fixed-loop at matched mean loops
numbers.value: halves drop at 1.25 loops; plateau at 2.70 loops
numbers.quote: adaptive looping outperforms fixed-loop inference at matched mean loop counts, halves the performance drop in a few-loop setting (at 1.25 loops), and reaches a comparable performance plateau earlier (at 2.70 loops).

numbers.what: Gap to next-best public model InternVL-U
numbers.quote: Notably, compared with the next-best model, InternVL-U, Looped-DiT B/16 achieves a 2.5-point higher avg. score with 6.5× fewer parameters.

limitations: Only ~260M MiniT2I MMDiT at 512x512 pixel space; fixed [6,5,6] split and training depth 4; deep supervision raises training compute; latent-reasoning evidence is behavioral only.
survey_notes: Strongest controlled evidence in diffusion: one of few vision papers with iso-param, iso-inference-FLOP, iso-training-FLOP and iso-effective-depth baselines in one table (Table 2). Mirrors LM findings that naive looping saturates/degrades beyond training depth and that loop-wise supervision (cf. Ouro, TRM deep supervision) is needed. New: attention-update magnitude control (gated attention / XSA) only inside the loop; loop depth vs denoising steps as two test-time axes. Table 1 is unmatched (public checkpoints).

title: Procedural Core: A Compact Recurrent Initialization for Vision Transformers
relevance_reason: A weight-tied (recurrent-middle-block) auxiliary ViT is trained on procedural data; its weights are unrolled to initialize an untied target model, so looping is used only as a compression/regularization device for initialization.
one_sentence: Trains a ViT-Tiny with tied middle blocks (3 unique blocks, depth 12) on procedural data, then unrolls and tiles it to initialize untied ViTs and LMs of any size, beating random init (+2.2 pp ImageNet ViT-B).
key_contributions: Recurrent auxiliary model compresses procedural-data warm-up into ~1M reusable weights expanded in depth (unroll) and width (tile).
Ablation: recurrence matters; a parameter-matched non-recurrent 3-layer auxiliary transfers much less.
Mechanism: recurrence broadens singular spectrum; structure sits in attention value/output path and suppresses high-norm tokens.

setup.model_sizes: ~1M-parameter core; targets up to ViT-Base 85M; GPT-2-style LM targets
setup.train_tokens_or_data: Procedural data (formal languages) for core; ImageNet-1K, CIFAR-100, DINO, FineWeb-Edu, CodeParrot for targets
setup.loops_train: middle block tied across blocks 2..L-1 with L=12
setup.baselines: Random init, mimetic/structured init, direct procedural warm-up of target, parameter-matched non-recurrent auxiliary
setup.benchmarks: ImageNet-1K, CIFAR-100, ADE20K, ImageNet-S, VOC07 CorLoc, NYUv2, FineWeb-Edu, CodeParrot

claims.claim: A recurrent auxiliary model transfers far better than a parameter-matched non-recurrent auxiliary model (+4.7% vs +1.7% over random init on CIFAR-100 ViT-Tiny).
claims.evidence_quote: Moreover, a parameter-matched 3-layer non-recurrent model yields only a +1.7% improvement over the default random initialization, compared with +4.7% for our recurrent one (Figure 5b).

claims.claim: Expanding a 1M-parameter recurrent core to initialize ViT-Base improves ImageNet top-1 by 2.2 pp over random init.
claims.regime: same target architecture and training; init only differs
claims.evidence_quote: For image classification, expanding a 1M-parameter core to initialize an 85M-parameter ViT-Base improves I MA GE N ET top-1 accuracy by 2.2 pp over standard random initialization.

numbers.what: Zero-shot segmentation ImageNet-S mAP random init vs Procedural Core
numbers.quote: In ViTs, we localize a key benefit in the suppression of high-norm tokens that produces substantial improvements in zero-shot segmentation (I MAGE N ET-S mAP 32.3 → 42.9)

numbers.what: Gain vs random init across target depth
numbers.quote: Figure 5c shows that the Procedural Core outperforms the default random initialization at every tested depth, with the gain increasing from +2.0% at 6 layers to +2.8% at 24 layers.

survey_notes: Not a looped model at deployment; looping is a training-time compression/regularizer whose weights are then untied (inverse of retrofitting dense to looped). Supports the Block-Recurrent Hypothesis line that ViT computation is compressible into a few reused blocks; useful for the 'what looping buys in vision' discussion (transferable structure, not test-time compute).

title: Recurrent-Depth VLA: Implicit Test-Time Compute Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models via Latent Iterative Reasoning
relevance_reason: Huginn-style prelude / weight-tied recurrent core / coda action head for a VLA, trained with randomized recurrence and TBPTT, with KL-based adaptive stopping.
one_sentence: Adds a Huginn-style recurrent action head (prelude, tied core with input injection, coda) on a Qwen2.5-0.5B VLA; LIBERO success climbs from 8.4% at 1 iteration to 92.6% at 8, with KL-convergence early stopping.
key_contributions: First VLA with weight-tied recurrent latent action head; noisy scratchpad init plus persistent input injection via concat adapter.
Training with Poisson log-normal sampled depth (mean 32) and TBPTT through last 8 iterations.
Adaptive stopping on KL/MSE between consecutive iterations; task-dependent iteration counts emerge; adaptive horizon execution.

setup.model_sizes: 0.5B (Qwen2.5-0.5B MiniVLA backbone) plus recurrent action head
setup.train_tokens_or_data: LIBERO and CALVIN robot demonstrations; real-world tasks
setup.loops_train: N ~ Poisson(e^tau)+1 with mu_rec = 32; TBPTT last 8 iterations
setup.baselines: End-to-end VLAs (OpenVLA, pi0, pi0.5), token-reasoning VLAs (ECoT, Fast-ThinkAct, 7B), same model at fewer iterations
setup.benchmarks: LIBERO (Spatial, Object, Goal, Long), CALVIN ABC->D, real robot

claims.claim: Test-time recurrence scaling: LIBERO average success rises log-linearly with iterations and saturates around 8-12.
claims.regime: same model, varying test-time iterations (no non-looped matched baseline)
claims.evidence_quote: Starting from near-random performance at Ninf = 1 (8.4% average), the model achieves substantial gains at each doubling of compute: 40.5% at Ninf = 2 (382% increase), 84.1% at Ninf = 4 (108% increase), and 92.6% at Ninf = 8 (10% increase).

claims.claim: KL-based adaptive stopping matches fixed-depth peak with 34% fewer iterations.
claims.regime: same model, adaptive vs fixed iterations
claims.evidence_quote: the Binary Adaptation strategy achieves 92.5% success rate (comparable to the 93.0% peak of fixed recurrence at N = 12) using an average of only k̄ = 7.93 iterations, which is a 34% reduction in compute.

claims.claim: RD-VLA (0.5B) beats prior VLAs including 7B token-reasoning methods on LIBERO; comparison against public models with different backbones/data.
claims.evidence_quote: RD-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance of 93.0% with fixed recurrence, significantly outperforming all prior methods, including the strong Fast-ThinkAct baseline (89.7%).

claims.claim: Depth generalization is bounded: beyond an optimal iteration count, recurrence can saturate or degrade.
claims.evidence_quote: extending recurrence beyond this number of iterations may lead to state saturation or performance degradation rather than continued refinement.

numbers.what: CALVIN ABC->D average chain length
numbers.quote: RD-VLA achieves the highest average chain length of 3.39, outperforming OpenVLA [22] (3.27) and all other baselines.

numbers.what: Inference speedup over prior reasoning VLAs
numbers.quote: replacing token-based reasoning with latent reasoning to achieve constant memory usage and up to 80× inference speedup over prior reasoning-based VLA models.

numbers.what: Adaptive exits per task category (tau=1e-4)
numbers.quote: Spatial tasks require more iterations (µ = 11.8) than Object (µ = 9.8)

limitations: Small 0.5B backbone; depth extrapolation beyond the optimal iteration count saturates or degrades; adaptive intervention design space unexplored.
survey_notes: Direct transfer of the Huginn recipe (prelude/core/coda, noisy state init, input injection, log-normal Poisson depth sampling, truncated BPTT, KL-based exit) to robotics; reproduces the LM pattern of saturating gains and limited extrapolation. No iso-param or iso-FLOP non-recurrent head baseline; all cross-model claims are unmatched.

title: Soft Mixture-of-Recursions: Going Deeper with Recursive Vision Transformers
relevance_reason: Recursive ViT that reuses shared intermediate blocks T times and softly mixes all recursion-step outputs per token.
one_sentence: SR-ViT groups intermediate DeiT blocks into coarse-to-fine recursive units, adds per-step linear step transforms and token-wise soft mixtures over all recursion outputs; ImageNet top-1 rises 79.83 to 82.48 from T=1 to 4 with +1.7M params.
key_contributions: Shows naive recursion in ViT helps at T=2 but drops below baseline at T=3; MoR-style hard depth selection also fails at T=3.
SoftMoR: token-wise learned weighted sum over all recursion-step outputs plus residual linear step transforms between steps.
Recursion depth as a scaling axis across ImageNet classification, COCO detection/instance segmentation, ADE20K segmentation.

setup.train_tokens_or_data: ImageNet-1K, DeiT protocol, 300 epochs from scratch
setup.baselines: DeiT-T/S/B, naive recursion, hard selection (MoR-style), recursive unit organizations
setup.benchmarks: ImageNet-1K, COCO (Mask R-CNN), ADE20K (UPerNet)

claims.claim: Recursion depth scales SR-ViT-S with near-constant parameters: top-1 79.83 (T=1) to 82.48 (T=4) with 1.7M extra parameters.
claims.evidence_quote: On ImageNet-1K, increasing recursion depth from 1 to 4 improves SR-ViT-S top-1 accuracy from 79.83% to 82.48% with only 1.7M additional parameters, outperforming the substantially larger DeiT-B while using approximately 27% of its parameters.

claims.claim: Against DeiT-B at slightly lower FLOPs, SR-ViT-S T=4 is more accurate at both 224 and 384 resolution.
claims.evidence_quote: Further increasing T to 4 raises the accuracy to 82.48% and 84.24% at 224 and 384, respectively, compared with 81.80% and 83.10% for DeiT-B, while still requiring slightly fewer FLOPs.

claims.claim: Naive recursion and MoR-style hard selection do not scale past T=2 in ViTs; using only the last (or selected) step's representation is the bottleneck.
claims.evidence_quote: When T is increased to 3, naive recursion drops to 79.17%, falling below the non-recursive baseline. This confirms that recursive reuse alone is not sufficient to reliably benefit from deeper computation.

numbers.what: Hard selection vs soft mixture at T=3 (SR-ViT-S top-1)
numbers.quote: However, when T is increased to 3, hard selection drops to 80.54%, while Soft Mixture continues to improve and reaches 82.45%.

numbers.what: Naive recursion coarse-to-fine T=2 top-1
numbers.quote: In contrast, the coarse-to-fine organization achieves the strongest result, improving ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy from 79.83% to 81.12%.

survey_notes: Argues token-level routing (MoR) transfers poorly to vision because visual tokens are processed jointly, not generated; replaces hard routing with soft aggregation over steps (a DenseNet-like history injection). Agrees with Looped-DiT (2609.40305) and Training Crossroads (2608.04879) that naive weight-tied depth stops helping in vision without intermediate-step usage/supervision. No iso-effective-depth deep untied baseline.

title: Training-Free Hidden-State Refinement for Flow-Matching Image Generators
relevance_reason: Training-free repetition of selected frozen DiT layers (damped residual updates, K rounds) inside each denoising call of flow-matching T2I models.
one_sentence: Repeats each layer in a mid-to-late range of a frozen flow-matching DiT K times with step size 1/K, gated to early sampling progress, plus 'Loop Guidance' extrapolating looped vs ordinary velocity; beats extra sampling steps at equal or lower time.
key_contributions: Damped per-layer residual looping (eta = 1/K) for frozen DiTs; dense and sparse-token variants; sampling-progress gating and layer-range selection.
Loop Guidance: CFG-like extrapolation between looped and ordinary vector fields.
Wall-clock comparison: internal looping beats adding outer Euler steps at equal or lower generation time.

setup.model_sizes: Scale-RAE DiT2.4B (Qwen1.5B), DiT9.8B, RAEv2 615M DDT
setup.train_tokens_or_data: none (training-free)
setup.loops_train: n/a
setup.loops_test: K = 4 default over layers [12, 27]; loop active for sampling progress in [0, 0.5]
setup.baselines: Same frozen models without looping, with 25/35/50 outer Euler steps
setup.benchmarks: GenEval, DPG-Bench, ImageReward, CLIP, OpenCLIP, PickScore

claims.claim: Internal layer looping at 25 steps beats a 50-step no-loop baseline on GenEval and DPG while being faster (wall-clock).
claims.regime: iso_param (same frozen weights); approximately iso-latency (lower time)
claims.evidence_quote: 0.8007 DPG-Bench in 2.1812 s, outperforming the 50-step no-loop baseline (0.4742 and 0.7738) while remaining faster than its 2.4032 s runtime.

claims.claim: Loop Guidance improves both primary metrics on all three frozen generators.
claims.evidence_quote: Loop Guidance further improves both primary metrics across all three tested models; on Scale-RAE DiT2.4B, it raises GenEval from 0.4471 to 0.5691 and DPG-Bench from 0.7656 to 0.8053.

claims.claim: Without guidance, transfer to RAEv2 is mixed (GenEval slightly drops); moderate K captures most gains and middle-to-late layers are better than early ones.
claims.evidence_quote: On RAEv2, both variants improve DPG-Bench and all auxiliary metrics but slightly reduce GenEval, so the unguided transfer result is mixed.

numbers.what: Sparse Token Loop time reduction vs Dense Token Loop
numbers.quote: Specifically, Sparse Token Loop reduces generation time by 22.6% on DiT2.4B and 39.6% on DiT9.8B relative to Dense Token Loop.

numbers.what: RAEv2 with Loop Guidance
numbers.quote: On RAEv2, Loop Guidance raises GenEval from 0.3829 to 0.4532 and DPGBench from 0.7131 to 0.7521 while improving every auxiliary metric.

limitations: Unguided transfer to RAEv2 mixed; guidance scale not tuned exhaustively; sparse variant slower at small (615M) scale.
survey_notes: Vision analogue of training-free layer repetition in LLMs; the damped step eta=1/K is a key difference from naive repetition (full updates cause excessive displacement). Agrees with Looped-DiT (2609.40305) that loop depth beats extra denoising steps under matched cost, here without any training and at 2.4B-9.8B. Middle-to-late layers best, consistent with LLM layer-duplication findings.

title: RecRec: Recursive Refinement for Sequential Recommendation
relevance_reason: TRM-style shared recursive core with inner/outer loops refining a persistent user-preference latent state, with a gated evidence-anchored correction.
one_sentence: RecRec refines a user-preference state with a weight-shared MLP core (T=7 outer steps x n=3 inner loops), a sigmoid gate interpolating back to the encoded history, and step-wise supervision; 3.9M-14M params beat SASRec, ReaRec and 7B LLM recommenders.
key_contributions: Recursive latent preference inference for sequential recommendation, inspired by TRM.
Evidence-anchored correction gate (interpolates refined state with original interaction encoding) to prevent drift.
Shows a peak in recursion steps (T=7) and that deeper unshared MLPs overfit.

setup.model_sizes: 3.9M-14M parameters
setup.train_tokens_or_data: Three benchmark datasets incl. Steam, Luxury Beauty, Video Games (leave-one-out)
setup.loops_train: T = 7 outer, n = 3 inner
setup.baselines: SASRec, UniRec, LightGCN, NGCF, ReaRec; LLM recommenders ALLMRec, TallRec (7B), GPT4Rec
setup.benchmarks: HR@k, NDCG@k

claims.claim: Recursion depth helps up to T=7 then degrades (over-refinement), mirroring LM overthinking.
claims.regime: iso_param (same model, varied T at training)
claims.evidence_quote: Increasing 𝑇 leads to consistent performance gains, with HR@1 peaking at 𝑇 = 7 (HR@1: 0.59). Beyond this point, performance degrades (e.g., HR@1 drops to 0.55 at 𝑇 = 13), indicating over-refinement.

claims.claim: Increasing unique depth of the core MLP beyond 5 layers overfits; recursion is the more parameter-efficient depth source.
claims.regime: unclear (deeper unshared core vs recursion, not FLOP-matched)
claims.evidence_quote: Increasing the depth to 10 layers (21.1M parameters) degrades performance (HR@1: 0.55), indicating overfitting to dataset-specific patterns rather than improved generalization.

claims.claim: RecRec beats sequential, graph, recursion-based and 7B LLM recommenders with far fewer parameters; baselines are separately configured models.
claims.evidence_quote: Remarkably, RecRec surpasses LLM-based models like ALLMRec and GPT4Rec despite a 99% smaller footprint (3.9M vs. 7B).

numbers.what: HR@1 on Steam at T=1 (single pass) vs T=7
numbers.quote: Our analysis on the Steam dataset shows that at 𝑇 = 1, RecRec reduces to a single-pass architecture (HR@1: 0.49).

survey_notes: Recsys transfer of TRM recipe (inner/outer recursion, deep supervision, state gating to input). Like LM looped models, gains peak then decline with more steps. Unlike LoopCTR (2604.19550), RecRec trains and tests at one fixed T and offers no FLOP-matched comparison.

title: LARES: Latent Reasoning for Sequential Recommendation
relevance_reason: Huginn-style pre-block plus recurrent core-block Transformer for sequential recommendation, with randomized log-normal Poisson depth, alignment pretraining and RL post-training.
one_sentence: LARES applies a recurrent core block (random-noise initial thought, input injection, LayerNorm) to all item tokens of a sequential recommender, samples depth from a log-normal Poisson in training, and adds trajectory/step alignment SSL plus GRPO-style RL post-training.
key_contributions: Depth-recurrent latent reasoning for sequential recommendation that refines all input tokens each step (vs last-token reasoning in ReaRec).
Self-supervised pretraining with trajectory-level and step-level alignment, then reinforcement post-training.
Plug-in compatibility with existing SR backbones (e.g., TedRec).

setup.model_sizes: pre-block and core-block each 1-2 Transformer layers; hidden size 256, embedding 64
setup.train_tokens_or_data: Four real-world datasets (incl. Amazon Instrument, Scientific)
setup.loops_train: k ~ Poisson(e^xi)+1 with mean k-bar+1, k-bar in {3,4,6}, truncated at 3 k-bar
setup.baselines: GRU4Rec, BERT4Rec, SASRec, FMLP-Rec, CL4SRec, DuoRec, BSARec, ERL/PRL/PRL++ (ReaRec family)
setup.benchmarks: Recall@k, NDCG@k

claims.claim: More reasoning steps help up to an optimum (3-4) and then degrade, analogous to overthinking.
claims.evidence_quote: performance initially improves with more reasoning steps but declines after reaching an optimal point, which is in line with the findings in ReaRec.

claims.claim: At comparable FLOPs (LARES 2+2x4 layers vs 10-layer SASRec), LARES adds about 10% latency; only latency, not accuracy, is reported at matched FLOPs.
claims.evidence_quote: The additional inference latency introduced by LARES remains moderate—approximately 10% higher than SASRec at comparable FLOPs.

claims.claim: LARES beats non-reasoning and reasoning SR baselines on four datasets; baselines use shared hyperparameters but are distinct architectures.
claims.regime: unmatched (shared embedding/hidden sizes, different architectures and compute)
claims.evidence_quote: Our proposed framework LARES outperforms all baselines, including both non-reasoning and reasoning models, by a large margin across all evaluation metrics on four datasets.

numbers.what: Optimal mean reasoning steps
numbers.quote: The optimal reasoning steps are 4 for Instrument and 3 for Scientific, highlighting the importance of selecting an appropriate reasoning depth for optimal performance.

numbers.what: Gain from plugging LARES into TedRec
numbers.quote: the superior TedRec model benefits from our framework, showing average improvements of 10.9% and 7.9% on the respective

limitations: Fixed reasoning depth for all sequences; excessive steps waste compute and can hurt; adaptive depth left to future work.
survey_notes: Recsys port of Huginn: pre-block + core, noisy initial state, randomized log-normal Poisson depth. Interest-peak (overthinking) phenomenon agrees with RecRec (2607.10541) and ReaRec. Notable: RL post-training of a looped model outside language. No accuracy result at matched FLOPs against a deeper SASRec.

title: Revisiting Implicit Models: Sparsity Trade-offs Capability in Weight-tied Model for Vision Tasks
relevance_reason: Benchmarks plain weight-tied (looped) vision layers against DEQs and explicit models; proposes per-iteration distinct sparse masks on the tied weight.
one_sentence: Shows plain unrolled weight-tied ResNet/ViT-like models beat DEQ variants and similar explicit models on CIFAR/ImageNet under the same budget, and that distinct fixed random sparse masks per iteration raise tied-layer capacity; width matters more than tied depth.
key_contributions: Fair benchmark: weight-tied (finite unroll, BPTT) beats DEQ / phantom-gradient DEQ in accuracy and time on vision.
Multi-mask weight-tied layers: deterministic random binary masks per iteration diversify a single tied weight.
Guidelines: increase width not tied depth; tied depth 6-8 is enough; wider and sparser preferred.

setup.model_sizes: Small and large ResNet-like and CCT/ViT-like models
setup.train_tokens_or_data: CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet32, ImageNet
setup.loops_train: tied depth e.g. 8 (DEQ comparison); 2-12 in trade-off study
setup.baselines: DEQ, phantom-gradient DEQ, explicit ResNet-20, CCT-7, dropout, same-mask sparse tied
setup.benchmarks: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet32, ImageNet

claims.claim: Finite unrolled weight-tied models outperform DEQ variants and similarly structured explicit models in accuracy and time.
claims.regime: same structure and hyperparameters as DEQ; same data
claims.evidence_quote: the weight-tied model could outperform most of the latest DEQ variants as well as explicit models in both performance and time complexity across various neural architectures.

claims.claim: Increasing tied depth helps far less than increasing width; a 12-deep tied model lags a 2-deep one that is 2x wider.
claims.regime: varied depth/width at fixed mask density (not FLOP matched)
claims.evidence_quote: a 12-depth multi-mask weight-tied model significantly lags behind a 2-depth multi-mask weight-tied which is 2 times wider.

numbers.what: Recommended tied depth
numbers.quote: Practical guide #1: The model width matters, rather than the depth of weight-tied layers: practically it is sufficient to use a depth of 6 or 8 in the weight-tied layers to ensure reasonably good performance.

survey_notes: Supports 'finite unroll beats fixed-point/implicit training' in vision, consistent with LM findings favoring BPTT over implicit gradients. Per-iteration random masks are an early form of relaxed sharing (step-specific parameters with zero extra params). Its 'width beats tied depth' guideline is a counterpoint to vision papers claiming recursion as a scaling axis (2607.00774).

title: Looped Actor: Depth-Recurrent Reasoning Models for Reinforcement Learning
relevance_reason: FPRM-style fixed-point looped transformer policy with KL-stabilization halting, trained with standard online/offline RL objectives through executed loops.
one_sentence: Looped Actor adapts the Fixed-Point Reasoning Model to RL policies, halting when consecutive action distributions' KL falls below a threshold; at 0.5M params it beats a 16x larger untied iso-FLOP stack on Boxoban and Rush Hour and ties it on OGBench.
key_contributions: Complexity-theoretic MDP family where state-adaptive policies need asymptotically less expected compute than any optimal fixed-runtime policy.
Looped transformer actor (and looped critic) with KL-based halting, trained with standard RL treating halting as non-differentiable.
Iso-parameter and iso-FLOP (16 untied blocks) baselines across 22 tasks in six environments; probes show plans emerge over loops.

setup.model_sizes: 0.5M (Looped Actor, Iso-Parameters), ~8M (Iso-FLOPs), ~1M DRC(3,3)
setup.train_tokens_or_data: Online RL (Boxoban, Rush Hour) and offline goal-conditioned RL (OGBench, 4 environments)
setup.loops_train: max 16
setup.baselines: Iso-Parameters (block applied once), Iso-FLOPs (16 untied blocks), DRC(3,3)
setup.benchmarks: Boxoban, Rush Hour, OGBench (20 tasks)

claims.claim: On planning-heavy puzzles, the 0.5M Looped Actor substantially outperforms an untied 16-block iso-FLOP baseline with 16x more parameters and DRC; the iso-parameter single-pass baseline barely learns.
claims.regime: iso_param and iso_train_flop / iso_effective_depth (16 untied blocks at max loops)
claims.evidence_quote: We report the success rate as a function of environment steps for Boxoban in Figure 1 and Rush Hour in Figure 2, showing the mean and standard deviation across three random seeds. Looped Actor substantially outperforms the Iso-FLOPs and DRC baselines despite having 2 to 16 times less

claims.claim: On less planning-heavy offline goal-conditioned control, Looped Actor ties or slightly beats the iso-FLOP baseline.
claims.evidence_quote: Looped Actor ties or slightly outperforms Iso-FLOPs in all four environments. Iso-Parameters performs substantially worse, achieving zero success on at least one downstream task in three of the four environments.

claims.claim: Compute allocation is structured: loops increase with remaining pushes and future optimal pushes become linearly decodable over loops.
claims.evidence_quote: For the Boxoban environment, we find that the computation allocation is structured: the number of loops increases with the number of remaining pushes and future optimal pushes become increasingly predictable from the latent state over successive loops.

numbers.what: Boxoban success vs untied 16x larger baseline
numbers.quote: On Boxoban, it achieves roughly twice the success rate of an untied transformer with 16 times as many parameters, while matching this baseline’s average performance across 20 offline goal-conditioned control tasks.

numbers.what: Model sizes
numbers.quote: We choose the hidden dimension of the blocks to be 128, resulting in a total of 0.5M parameters for Looped Actor and Iso-Parameters, and around 8M parameters for Iso-FLOPs.

limitations: No guarantee the learned policy is compute-optimal; computation is within a single environment step, no reasoning state carried across steps (memory/partial observability open).
survey_notes: Cleanest RL evidence with both iso-param and iso-FLOP (iso-effective-depth) baselines. Looped beats untied deeper model on planning tasks (generalization/data-efficiency advantage of tying, consistent with algorithmic-task results in LM literature) and ties elsewhere. Note the 'Iso-FLOPs' baseline matches compute only at max loops; with adaptive halting, Looped Actor uses fewer FLOPs.

title: Depth through recurrence: Looped transformers for flow-matching TTS
relevance_reason: Controlled comparison of seven weight-reuse layouts (cycle, sequence, prefix/middle/suffix partial loops) at matched executed depth in F5-TTS.
one_sentence: Trains seven F5-TTS Small layouts with 18 block calls each; SEQUENCE (each of 9 blocks applied twice consecutively) keeps WER competitive at 47.1% fewer params, more sharing hurts, and placement of the shared segment matters most at few sampling steps.
key_contributions: Iso-effective-depth (18 calls) comparison of sharing amount, order (cycle vs sequence) and placement (prefix/middle/suffix) in flow-matching TTS.
Interaction between loop layout and sampling budget: prefix vs suffix similar at 32 steps but diverge at 4 steps.
Call-ablation shows unshared early calls are most removal-sensitive; shared interior calls are robust.

setup.model_sizes: Baseline 158.0M (18 unique blocks); CYCLE/SEQUENCE 9x2 83.6M; CYCLE 6x3 58.8M; Prefix/Middle/Suffix 108.4M
setup.train_tokens_or_data: LibriTTS (train-clean-100/360, train-other-500), 500k updates, one run per layout
setup.loops_train: 2 or 3 visits of shared segment; 18 executed calls
setup.baselines: Unshared 18-block Baseline
setup.benchmarks: Seed-TTS test-en, LibriSpeech-PC (WER via Whisper large-v3, SIM-o, UTMOS)

claims.claim: At matched executed depth (18 calls), SEQUENCE 9x2 matches the unshared baseline's WER with 47.1% fewer parameters (differences not significant; not equivalence).
claims.evidence_quote: SEQUENCE uses 83.6M parameters versus Baseline’s 158.0M, a 47.1% reduction, with the same 18 block calls. At 32 steps, its WER is 2.03/2.26% on Seed-TTS/LibriSpeech-PC versus Baseline’s 2.23/2.29% (Table 1).

claims.claim: More sharing has limits: cycling 6 blocks three times raises WER vs cycling 9 blocks twice.
claims.evidence_quote: CYCLE 9 × 2 has 32-step WER of 2.60/2.14%; CYCLE 6 × 3 saves another 24.8M parameters but raises WER to 2.96/2.65% and lowers SIM-o on both datasets.

claims.claim: Placement of the shared segment interacts with the sampling budget: suffix sharing is much worse at 4 steps.
claims.evidence_quote: At four steps, Suffix instead exceeds Prefix by 3.44 pp, 95% CI [2.77, 4.14], and 5.97 pp [3.69, 8.70].

numbers.what: Peak inference memory reduction from 9x2 sharing
numbers.quote: CYCLE 9 × 2 and SEQUENCE 9 × 2 reduce peak allocated memory from 877 to 574 MB (34.5%); CYCLE 6 × 3 and the partial loops use 474 and 675 MB.

numbers.what: Cycle vs sequence at matched size and depth (Seed-TTS 32-step WER)
numbers.quote: At matched size and depth, SEQUENCE lowers 32-step Seed-TTS WER from CYCLE’s 2.60 to 2.03, a paired change of −0.57 pp

limitations: One training run per layout (training-seed variance not measured); F5-TTS Small only; no visit-index embedding or auxiliary supervision tested; sampling time unchanged (no speedup).
survey_notes: Speech evidence that looping saves parameters/memory but not latency at matched executed depth. Cycle vs sequence (repeat-each-layer) order matters, echoing Takase & Kiyono in MT. Keeping early blocks unshared (sandwich) matters, consistent with LM prelude findings. Careful statistics (paired CIs) make it a reliable iso-effective-depth data point.

title: DeepJEPA: Scaling World Models from Within
relevance_reason: Weight-tied recurrent transition cell inside a JEPA world model with a learned per-candidate, per-step continue head for adaptive internal depth during CEM planning.
